title: Neutrophil heterogeneity in immune regulation- Bioinformatics Core - Hidalgo
text: Bioinformatics Core The Bioinformatics Core aims to facilitate the use of analytical and computational pipelines for transcriptomic and imaging applications, provide a centralized and standardized analysis and interpretation of the data, and improve the cost-effectiveness of the transcriptomic analyses. The Core will provide 1) a centralized resource for bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) for all Projects using the expertise of Dr. Hidalgo’s team and the extensive expertise and instrumentation at the YCGA (Yale Center for Genome Analysis); 2) unify procedures and protocols for sample processing; 3) provide standardized analytical pipelines for computational analysis of transcriptomic data, an aspect of particular relevance given the challenges associated with the analysis of the neutrophil transcriptome; 4) provide a platform for comparison of the transcriptional profiles generated herein with datasets and other resources that are unique to this Program, including the unpublished NeutroMap: 5) enable in vivo clonal tracing of the populations of interest through genetic barcoding in the DARLIN mouse, a powerful tool generated by our collaborator Dr. Camargo. This includes processing of the samples and downstream computational analyses; 5) supporting 4D imaging and downstream computational analyses for behavioral profiling of neutrophils, using tools recently established by the Hidalgo lab; 6) provide a centralized platform for the development of computational tools on demand (such as inference of regulatory networks, transcriptional dynamics and cell-cell interactions), and technical assistance for all Projects of this Program. Overall, the Bioinformatics Core will significantly reduce cost in sample processing and provide access to expert bioinformaticians, thereby enhancing the quality and productivity of the Program.

title: Cellular and circuit basis for flexible control of sensory acquisition
text:
The goal of the proposed research is to understand how multiple levels of motor control enable the brain to
shape our behavior to our sensory experience of our surroundings. Here we will study specific neural circuitry
in the fruit fly antennal mechanosensory system to probe motor behavior in response to active sensory
information gathered by the antenna during behavior. Discoveries made in our model system will aid our
understanding of how these brain circuits operate in the brain, and how disruptions in these same circuits
cause human disease.

title: Mechanisms of a conserved niche endothelial program directing hematopoietic stem cell migration
text:
Bone marrow transplantation offers a potentially curable treatment for numerous diseases of the blood and
immune system, including cancer, yet it remains a high-risk procedure that can leave patients
immunocompromised and vulnerable to infection for months post-transplantation. A better understanding of the
pathways and mechanisms that guide circulating donor stem cells into the recipient’s bone marrow, which must
happen before the stem cells can regenerate a new immune system, could inform novel therapeutic strategies
to accelerate stem cell migration and immune system recovery following a transplant. My proposed studies
fulfill this critical unmet clinical need by elucidating the fundamental cellular and molecular mechanisms within
the specialized cells of the vasculature that facilitate stem cell migration into the bone marrow.

title: Longitudinal Impact of Clonal Hematopoiesis on Aging Outcomes and Risk Prediction in the REasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke Study
text:
Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminant potential (CH) is a common abnormality detected in peripheral blood
induced by age-related DNA mutations, which give rise to proinflammatory cells. CH is associated with
multiple adverse aging outcomes making it a promising biomarker for age-related diseases, but has been less
studied in representative populations for disease prevention. We propose to measure CH over time in the
30,239 Black and White participants of the REasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke study to
examine risk factors for CH as well as evaluate it as a predictor of common age-related diseases.

title: Integrating Chemical Genetic Approaches with Precision Genome Editing
text:
Chemical genetics is powerfully enabling for biological discovery and therapeutics development. We propose to
leverage breakthroughs in precision genome-editing technologies and multi-omics to transform chemical genetic
approaches, allowing us to illuminate small molecule mechanism and endogenous protein structure-function at
scale and in high resolution. By applying these innovative approaches to critical and diverse protein targets, we
expect to advance our fundamental understanding of drug mechanism of action and protein complex structure
and function.

title: Disease Model Development and Phenotyping Project
text: The goal of the Disease Model Development and Phenotyping Project (DMP) is to develop novel mouse models of late-onset Alzheimer’s disease (LOAD), to deeply phenotype these models, and to make all data and mouse strains available to enable researchers to select the optimal mouse model and timepoints for therapeutic and intervention testing, as well as for the testing of hypotheses concerning mechanisms of LOAD. During the past five years, we have generated and deeply phenotyped mice with one component of our base genetic platform in which the Aß region of the App gene was humanized, and we have recently introduced the second component, a humanized MAPT (TAU) locus produced via gene-replacement. We have also used CRISPR and genome replacement to model and validate nine GWAS identified LOAD risk-variants and have analyzed mice with each variant both on a wild-type and 5xFAD background to determine their effects on plaque generation and damage exerted on the brain in response to pathology. In this continuation, we will use the results of these analyses, plus input from the FGBDMC and the literature, to identify combinations of LOAD risk variants most likely to phenocopy LOAD and introduce them on two complementary hAb-KI, hTAU, hAPOE4 platform lines, designed to mimic sub-types of AD that have been recently defined. These models will be characterized across their lifespans to evaluate the effects of variants on the development of pathologies and subsequent tissue damage in combination with aging. The UCI MODEL-AD group utilizes a comprehensive approach to evaluate these LOAD mouse models, which includes behavioral/cognitive assessment, electrophysiological analysis, super- resolution synaptic imaging, neuroimaging, bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, single cell level spatial transcriptomic analysis, proteomics, and microbiome and metabolome investigations including screening for novel biofluid markers associated with progression to LOAD. UCI MODEL-AD will leverage the resources of our NIA-funded Alzheimer’s Disease Research Center combined with the Accelerating Medicines Partnership Program for Alzheimer's Disease (AMP-AD) and other human AD datasets to facilitate alignment of data obtained from these mouse models to the human condition to identify the best mouse models for use by the international AD research community. All data and models will be made available without restrictions, via The Jackson Labs (JAX), and data will be explorable via the modeladexplorer.org website, and raw data freely available for download via the AD Knowledge Portal.

title: Elucidating Drug Interactomes for Cardiac Protection by SGLT2 Inhibitors
text:
Heart failure is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, and the off-target mechanisms by which
sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiac protection in this context remain largely elusive.
Defining the SGLT2 inhibitor “interactome” – how it affects gene expression, metabolite abundance, and forms
direct protein interactions – presents an opportunity to resolve protective pathways. This proposal uses human
induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)- derived cardiovascular cells and three-dimensional tissue engineering to
identify molecular interplay conferred by SGLT2 inhibition in health and disease, with proteomic interrogation
and animal validation to identify cardioprotective targets.

title: Neural Control of NREM Sleep in the Medulla
text:
In this proposal, we make use of optogenetic and chemogenetic tools, in vivo calcium imaging,
RNA-seq, viral-based circuit tracing, and genetic targeting techniques to dissect the neural
circuits that control sleep behavior. By identifying novel sleep-inducing neurons in the brain,
the work presented in this research proposal will lead to a mechanistic understanding of
sleep behavior and may provide valuable information for developing new treatments for
various human sleep disorders, such as insomnia.

title: Development of a web-based predictive model of nanoparticle delivery to tumors by integrating physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling with artificial intelligence
text:
Many laboratory studies have demonstrated that nanoparticle-based drug formulations (i.e., nanomedicines)
are effective in diagnostics and therapeutics of cancer in mice, but the translation of animal study findings to
clinical success in humans is limited, partially, because of a low delivery efficiency of nanoparticles to the
tumor and a lack of a robust computer model that can predict the tumor delivery efficiency of nanoparticles and
the carried drug and extrapolate the results from animals to humans. This project is relevant to public health
because the knowledge, data, and computer models gained from the proposed research will answer a key
question of whether there is a sex difference in tumor delivery of nanoparticles and will also improve our
understanding of the key determinants of tissue distribution and tumor delivery of nanoparticles and the carried
drug, which are essential for the design of effective nanomedicines. In addition, the proposed research will
create a publicly available web dashboard that enables researchers to predict delivery efficiency of
nanoparticles and the carried drug to tumor and major organs in one animal species and then extrapolate to
another animal species, which will greatly help to reduce animal experimentation in nanomedicine studies and
accelerate clinical translation of nanoparticle-based anticancer drug formulations to benefit cancer patients.

title: Role of exosomal SPHK1 in ovarian cancer progression
text:
While immunotherapies have transformed cancer treatment strategies, a robust response has not been
observed in ovarian cancer. Our studies are geared towards understanding how manipulating
sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) signaling influences PD-L1 expression, which can be used to produce a
favorable immune microenvironment amenable for ovarian cancer immunotherapy.

title: Investigating single cell transcriptomics and epigenetic regulation to enable stress-resistant brain network activity
text:
Stress contributes substantially to the onset and progression of several psychiatric disorders including major
depressive disorder (MDD); an important hurdle for developing effective therapies to treat such disorders is to
identify underlying vulnerabilities that predispose the pre-stressed brain to dysfunctional responses to stress.
Here we use a brain-wide electrical network in a mouse model of chronic social stress to dissect the cellular and
molecular contributors to a stress-vulnerable brain state prior to the onset of chronic-stress induced dysfunction.
Such an approach has the potential to 1) help identify prophylactic treatments to prevent the development of
stress-related disorders, 2) better understand the causal mechanisms of stress-induced maladaptation, and 3)
identify molecules as potential targets to augment resilient brain network activity.

title: Determining the contribution of Natural Killer Cells to the in vivo clearance of Plasmodium erythrocytic stage parasites
text:
We are translating human correlative findings suggesting that natural killer (NK) cells play a beneficial role in
malaria infection into a definitive in vivo test of their ability to clear parasites in mice. If confirmed, this would
indicate that NK cells enhance the neutralizing efficacy of antibodies. These findings would reshape our
understanding of how antibodies protect against the blood stage of infection and could inform the development
of improved therapeutic strategies to better protect children from malaria.

title: Transcriptomics, pathobiology, and cardiac event in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
text:
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is the most common genetic cardiac disease and causes a variety
of major cardiovascular events such as arrhythmias, heart failure, stroke, and sudden cardiac
death; however, effective pharmacotherapies to prevent disease manifestation or cardiovascular
events are not available. In an ongoing, large multi-center cohort of patients with hypertrophic
cardiomyopathy, the investigators will define the role of signaling pathway dysregulation in the
disease pathobiology and the development of cardiovascular events by performing parallel
transcriptomic profiling in both myocardium and plasma. This research has the potential to
identify molecular targets for the prevention of disease manifestation and progression, and to
offer novel approaches to specify high-risk subpopulations that benefit most from preventive
interventions.

title: Computational Modeling of Lineage Decisions using Single-cell Data
text:
Cellular differentiation is the process through which individual stem cells generate a multitude of cell types, each
with distinct form and function. The proposed project aims to illuminate the mechanisms that drive differentiation
through data-driven modeling of high-throughput single-cell data. A comprehensive understanding of such
mechanisms will provide a basis to decipher the dysregulation in disease and significantly boost the potential of
cell engineering to produce treatment-grade cells and tissues.

title: A hERG1 potassium channel subdomain is trafficked to the cardiac nucleus: mechanisms and targets of the hERG1NP
text:
hERG1 is a voltage gated potassium channel that regulates cardiac function. We identified a subdomain of the hERG1
potassium channel, hERG1NP, that is targeted to the nuclei of immature cardiac cells. From the nucleus, the hERG1NP alters
gene expression as well as hERG1 channel gating and expression. The approaches that we implement in this grant will
define the mechanisms that regulate hERG1NP function and its impact on potassium channel activity and cell function, which
will improve the accuracy of predicting the pathogenicity of hERG1NP variants and may inform future drug design targeting
this channel.

title: Synthetic Biology Approaches to Engineer Lactococcus lactis for Targeted Delivery of Therapeutic Lasso Peptides
text:
The use of bacteria as vehicles for drug delivery is a revolutionary novel approach for therapeutic purposes.
The current proposal aims to develop a bacteria-based system for the targeted delivery of active natural
products using engineered Lactococcus lactis as the platform to express biosynthetic gene clusters encoding
active compounds for in situ production and delivery.

title: Cellular and molecular mechanisms governing stem cell resilience
text:
Stem cells can regenerate damaged tissue, but their function often declines with age due to overuse. The
proposed research aims to study planarian flatworms—animals which possess highly resilient, long-lasting
stem cells—to uncover the mechanisms responsible for maintaining their inexhaustible regenerative capacity.
Understanding these mechanisms could lead to new strategies for enhancing stem cell function in organisms
with less pronounced regenerative abilities, including humans.

title: Artificial Intelligence Tool to Optimize Organ Transplantation Outcomes (Transplant-AI)
text:
The organ transplantation process has many inefficiencies and significant issues that result in
less than optimal patient outcomes and impacts to valuable clinical resources. Our product,
TransplantAI, aims to transform the organ matching process. By utilizing advanced AI
algorithms, large proprietary datasets and access to world renowned medical experts at leading
transplant centers and organ procurement organizations (OPOs), the InformAI team plans to
address limitations of current transplant analytic models by enhancing data insights into organ
discard, waitlist mortality and post transplant survival.

title: Clinical Research Sites for the Network of Excellence in Neuroscience Clinical Trials (NeuroNEXT sites) (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)
text: Over the past four years, we have established a highly efficient team and strong infrastructure at our combined CUIMC-WCM site capable of responding to the challenges of completing 4 phase 2 trials and 3 active trials. Six assistant professors completed 1-year NNEXT fellowships. If awarded, we will recruit diverse participants in early phase trials including ultra-rare genetic disorders and expand the fellowship.

title: Optimizing methods of clinical sample processing for scRNA-seq and mechanistic studies in sepsis to enable reliable, reproducible, and high-yield multi-center collection efforts
text:
Sepsis is a common and deadly disease characterized by organ failure due to a dysfunctional immune response
to infection; yet there is much we do not understand about the immune response to sepsis because of practical
limitations in studying it broadly in humans. Our goal is to optimize and validate a simple whole blood
cryoprecipitation method using 2 mL of patient blood that we developed to make deep immune profiling via single
cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) broadly available for multicenter clinical investigations in sepsis. This will
enable detailed studies of broad and diverse populations of sepsis patients to discover how each individual
immune cell type is responding to infection, which will greatly expand our understanding of underlying disease
mechanisms, facilitate development of novel immune-directed therapies, and characterize patient subtypes by
their immune response signature that might respond favorably to certain therapies over others.
